architecture_independence_criterion.boundary: This is an exact audit of the pinned structured artifact, not proof that arbitrary future prose lacks hidden architectural commitments.
architecture_independence_criterion.semantics: External contract truth is unchanged by bijective reminting of an audit-only implementation label.

operational_contract.allowed_info: current semantic cut c(X_t) and calibration context; no privileged future or oracle side channel
operational_contract.inputs: raw sensor stream X_t with declared sensor type, noise model, bandwidth and latency contract
operational_contract.required_behaviour: emit response r_t that distinguishes obligation-relevant equivalence classes of X_t under declared noise
operational_contract.resource_metric: sensor bandwidth, encoding bits |c|, and transformation cost tau for the perception map
operational_contract.success_metric: exact 0/1 correctness on the obligation partition, or L2/0-1 error within declared tolerance epsilon

operational_contract.allowed_info: context-conditioned routing decision plus the selected source; no simultaneous full product
operational_contract.inputs: multi-source stream (x0,x1,context q) with finite access constraint (only one source exposed per step)
operational_contract.required_behaviour: route the obligation-relevant source for the current context q (achieve context-dependent accuracy above every fixed route)
operational_contract.resource_metric: routing decision cost c_r plus accessed source width versus exposure cost c_e(|U|-E|E_x|)
operational_contract.success_metric: exact accuracy on x_q obligation: 8/8 routed vs 6/8 best fixed source (GG55 census)

operational_contract.allowed_info: bounded persistent state S_working carried through the delay; no external store access during delay
operational_contract.inputs: transient cue that must be retained across a short interference-filled delay before response
operational_contract.required_behaviour: maintain the cue distinction through the delay and emit it correctly at probe time despite interference
operational_contract.resource_metric: persistent state cardinality |S_working|, maintenance transformation cost, and interference susceptibility
operational_contract.success_metric: exact reproduction accuracy after delay, or within-tolerance recall; must degrade monotonically with load and interference

operational_contract.allowed_info: episodic store plus cue-driven retrieval channel; no semantic summary alone suffices for the probe
operational_contract.inputs: autobiographical event (what, where, when, context) presented once with spatiotemporal tags
operational_contract.required_behaviour: reinstate the specific bound episode from a partial cue, distinguishing it from similar episodes
operational_contract.resource_metric: episodic entry count N_t, encoding/retrieval cost, and consolidation cost to long-term store
operational_contract.success_metric: cued recall precision and source discrimination (hit rate vs false reinstatement) on the obligation partition

operational_contract.allowed_info: compressed semantic store abstracting away episode identity; no verbatim trace of each encounter retained
operational_contract.inputs: repeated encounters with category members carrying stable statistical regularities across episodes
operational_contract.required_behaviour: answer category-level probes (generalisation, property inference) by de-duplicating shared structure across episodes
operational_contract.resource_metric: semantic code size, abstraction cost, and retrieval transformation tau
operational_contract.success_metric: generalisation accuracy to held-out members and false-memory resistance on the semantic quotient

operational_contract.allowed_info: compiled procedural routine (production/circuit/policy) retrieved without declarative recall of instruction traces
operational_contract.inputs: repeated practice on a sensorimotor or cognitive skill under a stable transformation requirement
operational_contract.required_behaviour: execute the skill faster and with lower online transformation cost after compilation, with retained accuracy
operational_contract.resource_metric: compiled code size, compilation (search) cost, and online execution cost
operational_contract.success_metric: execution latency and online tau reduction at matched accuracy; interference/transfer cost to other skills

operational_contract.allowed_info: retrieval transformation over the store plus current cue; store coverage and reliability declared
operational_contract.inputs: probe cue plus external/persistent store with residual obligation-relevant distinctions
operational_contract.required_behaviour: return the obligation-relevant residual that the parametric state alone lacks, within the retrieval cut capacity
operational_contract.resource_metric: index size, retrieval query cost tau_retrieve, and communication cut width
operational_contract.success_metric: residual accuracy gain over no-retrieval baseline at matched store coverage; retrieval precision/recall

operational_contract.allowed_info: offline replay channel and consolidation transformation that restructures traces into semantic/procedural form
operational_contract.inputs: episodic traces accumulated over episodes plus a stable long-term store with replay opportunity
operational_contract.required_behaviour: integrate traces so later retrieval needs fewer active states (saving t - ceil(log2 N_t)) while preserving joint retention
operational_contract.resource_metric: replay steps, consolidation transformation cost, and resulting long-term code size
operational_contract.success_metric: retention accuracy after consolidation at reduced active-state budget; CSR-1 minimum M*_t = N_t preserved

operational_contract.allowed_info: policy choosing which distinctions to merge/drop; no unbounded state expansion allowed
operational_contract.inputs: accumulated distinctions that outgrow the state budget or become obligation-irrelevant under drift
operational_contract.required_behaviour: drop exactly those distinctions whose loss costs least future obligation error, respecting the forgetting threshold
operational_contract.resource_metric: retained state cardinality after forgetting and relearning cost for dropped distinctions if they recur
operational_contract.success_metric: future expected loss after forgetting versus random or no-forgetting baseline at matched budget

operational_contract.allowed_info: predictive response representation (world model) plus current belief state; no oracle future observation
operational_contract.inputs: temporal stream with predictable suffix given a learned world model and current state estimate
operational_contract.required_behaviour: emit the predictive response that minimises obligation-relevant surprise (next observation or latent consequence)
operational_contract.resource_metric: model code size, inference tau, and belief-state maintenance cost
operational_contract.success_metric: next-step predictive accuracy and calibration of forecast uncertainty on the registered stream

operational_contract.allowed_info: naming/boundary decision that groups instances into a class when PVR-3 reuse threshold is crossed
operational_contract.inputs: instance stream where some distinctions are reusable across future obligations and others are idiosyncratic
operational_contract.required_behaviour: form a new concept (name + boundary) exactly when reuse amortises naming cost; place boundaries at the bang-bang optimum
operational_contract.resource_metric: number of concepts retained, boundary description bits, and retrieval cost per use
operational_contract.success_metric: reuse-weighted accuracy: concept-assisted future probe accuracy minus naming cost, versus no-concept baseline

operational_contract.allowed_info: compositional code where each primitive's code is reused; no holistic codebook larger than the product
operational_contract.inputs: structured query whose meaning is a product of primitive meanings (e.g. a* -> b* with constraints)
operational_contract.required_behaviour: compose primitive answers into the correct product response without enumerating the full product table
operational_contract.resource_metric: codebook size (|primitives| not |product|) and composition transformation cost
operational_contract.success_metric: accuracy on held-out compositions (systematic generalisation) and description-length saving versus holistic enumeration

operational_contract.allowed_info: skill library of retained sub-quotients; option/macro that compiles the subsequence into one decision
operational_contract.inputs: action sequence where a contiguous subsequence recurs across tasks with shared dynamics
operational_contract.required_behaviour: chunk the recurring subsequence into a skill when PVR-3 threshold is crossed; second-level chunking self-limits as C lowers
operational_contract.resource_metric: skill description size, skill retrieval cost, and retained state per level
operational_contract.success_metric: planning and execution cost reduction across tasks versus flat search; skill reuse count and transfer

operational_contract.allowed_info: internal simulation (model-based lookahead) consuming tau; no oracle rollout beyond the declared model fidelity
operational_contract.inputs: current state, action set, transition model, and goal predicate over future states (plus horizon/budget)
operational_contract.required_behaviour: return a trajectory whose next action is optimal under the model and stop expanding when no expansion changes the action or pays (EVC <= 0)
operational_contract.resource_metric: simulation steps tau, search frontier size, and model-query cost
operational_contract.success_metric: goal attainment rate and action optimality under the model; planning-depth vs accuracy tradeoff

operational_contract.allowed_info: probe proposal plus Bayesian or worst-case uncertainty measure over the obligation-relevant quotient
operational_contract.inputs: uncertain world/task distribution with probes whose answers have declared cost and downstream value
operational_contract.required_behaviour: select the probe whose expected reduction in obligation-relevant uncertainty minus resources is maximal (non-negative to act)
operational_contract.resource_metric: probe execution cost, search/experiment budget, and time to decision
operational_contract.success_metric: information gain per cost and downstream decision accuracy versus no-probe or random-probe baseline

operational_contract.allowed_info: causal identification machinery (back-door, do-calculus) and supported intervention evaluation; no privileged counterfactual labels
operational_contract.inputs: observational distribution P(X,Y) plus admissible intervention set and declared graph class
operational_contract.required_behaviour: distinguish P(Y|X) from P(Y|do(X)) and report identifiability correctly within the declared graph scope
operational_contract.resource_metric: graph search cost and identification proof length
operational_contract.success_metric: identification correctness on the registered SCM (CAU-5a tables) and sign/bound accuracy where identifiable

operational_contract.allowed_info: counterfactual computation (twin network / abduction-action-prediction) within the declared response-table scope
operational_contract.inputs: observed outcome under an actual intervention plus the structural model and response table
operational_contract.required_behaviour: compute P(Y_x' | x, y) or PN correctly where rung-3 is identifiable and abstain where only bounds exist
operational_contract.resource_metric: counterfactual inference cost and model specification burden
operational_contract.success_metric: counterfactual probability correctness on W5A/W5B (PN 1/2 vs 1) and bound soundness where not point-identified

operational_contract.allowed_info: derived confidence conf=|adequate|/|S|, error likelihood 1-conf, and expected value of cognition EVC
operational_contract.inputs: internal decision state: surviving candidate set S, adequate-action sets Gamma(w), pending probes and costs
operational_contract.required_behaviour: gate action with confidence=1 iff C(S) nonempty, continue probing iff EVC>0, and select among reasoning strategies by worst-case total value
operational_contract.resource_metric: metacognitive computation (EVC evaluation) and strategy-register evaluation cost
operational_contract.success_metric: calibration (adequacy rate at each conf level equals that level) and decision accuracy per cost

operational_contract.allowed_info: agent model as retained state predicting the other's policy (copycat/contrarian/beauty-contest) plus belief hierarchy of bounded depth
operational_contract.inputs: observations of another agent's actions plus declared ecology of that agent's incentives and information
operational_contract.required_behaviour: predict and best-respond to the other's policy where opponent-type matters; recurse to the exact closure depth (e.g. beauty ladder depth 3)
operational_contract.resource_metric: agent-model state size, inference tau, and recursion depth cost
operational_contract.success_metric: joint payoff versus fixed-policy baseline; opponent-type prediction accuracy; recursion depth correctness

operational_contract.allowed_info: protocol over the shared semantic cut; messages conditioned on local observations and common ground
operational_contract.inputs: shared obligation and context plus a declared message channel with width/cost/noise contract
operational_contract.required_behaviour: implement the distributed semantic cut: send exactly the distinctions the joint obligation requires, no more and no fewer
operational_contract.resource_metric: message width (symbols), channel uses, and protocol description cost
operational_contract.success_metric: distributed task success rate at matched message width; information-theoretic efficiency (bits per required distinction)

operational_contract.allowed_info: observation of expert behaviour plus a correspondence mapping between demonstrator and imitator action spaces
operational_contract.inputs: demonstration trajectory of an expert (state-action sequence) under a declared embodiment mapping
operational_contract.required_behaviour: reproduce the expert's policy (not just trajectory) in the imitator's embodiment, generalising beyond the demo states
operational_contract.resource_metric: demonstration count, correspondence search cost, and imitation learning compute
operational_contract.success_metric: policy fidelity on held-out states and task success after imitation versus from-scratch learning

operational_contract.allowed_info: pedagogical actions (demonstration, instruction, scaffolding, feedback) selected to maximise learner's future obligation success
operational_contract.inputs: learner state estimate plus a teachable procedure whose learning curve and transfer are declared
operational_contract.required_behaviour: choose teaching interventions that minimise learner's time-to-mastery at matched teaching cost; respect n > 1 + S/(C-U) break-even
operational_contract.resource_metric: teaching actions/instructions sent and teacher planning cost
operational_contract.success_metric: learner sample efficiency and post-teaching transfer accuracy versus no-teaching or random-teaching baseline

operational_contract.allowed_info: cultural store (artifacts, language, institutions) transmitted with declared fidelity; no unbounded individual memory assumed
operational_contract.inputs: population of learners plus a transmission channel with fidelity contract and generational turnover
operational_contract.required_behaviour: ratchet complexity across generations so the population's frontier exceeds any single lifetime's reachable set
operational_contract.resource_metric: population size, transmission fidelity overhead, and cultural store size
operational_contract.success_metric: generational increase in task complexity solved and retention of prior gains (no cultural loss)

operational_contract.allowed_info: self-observation channel (interoception / execution trace) and a self-model representation with declared fidelity
operational_contract.inputs: own internal state and process traces plus a probe family over self-state
operational_contract.required_behaviour: maintain a self-model that correctly predicts own future responses and resource needs within the probe family
operational_contract.resource_metric: self-monitoring cost, self-model state size, and update frequency
operational_contract.success_metric: self-prediction accuracy and resource-estimation calibration on the declared self-probe set

capability_definitions.note: The generic phrase 'architecture edit' in self-improvement names an allowed intervention, not a required implementation family.

operational_contract.allowed_info: introspective evaluation and a governed self-modification channel with verification gate
operational_contract.inputs: own performance history plus a declared improvement operator (self-rewrite, hyperparameter update, architecture edit)
operational_contract.required_behaviour: apply self-modifications that improve the capability frontier or resource efficiency and pass the verification gate
operational_contract.resource_metric: self-modification search cost, verification cost, and risk of regression
operational_contract.success_metric: frontier expansion or resource reduction after self-modification versus no-modification baseline at matched verification

operational_contract.allowed_info: tool-call channel plus tool inputs/outputs; internal state alone does not contain the tool's information or transformation
operational_contract.inputs: task requiring an external transformation (calculator, code executor, database, actuator) with declared tool contract
operational_contract.required_behaviour: compose with the tool so joint system achieves the obligation while internal tau is reduced by the tool's contribution
operational_contract.resource_metric: tool-call count, tool latency/cost, and tool-interface description overhead
operational_contract.success_metric: task success rate with tool versus without, at matched tool-call budget and communication cost

operational_contract.allowed_info: collective state, joint action selection, and coordination protocol over the social-topology cut structure
operational_contract.inputs: population of agents with overlapping or coupled obligations and a declared social topology and communication contract
operational_contract.required_behaviour: achieve the coupled obligation that no single agent can achieve alone, with coordination cost correctly accounted
operational_contract.resource_metric: communication volume, coordination rounds, and collective state size
operational_contract.success_metric: collective success rate versus independent-agent baseline; coordination overhead and consensus quality

ceilings.falsifier: An exact in-scope controller with S<K states solves all K pairwise distinguishable obligations with zero error.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For arbitrary history-class and state sets, zero-error separation induces an injection from obligation classes into registered persistent response states; hence |H/~| <= |Q|. Tight realization requires a chosen representative/code for each class.
historical_assumptions: finite history quotient
no external memory or hidden side channel
future observations do not re-separate histories already merged by the controller
zero-error registered obligation
ceilings.historical_bound: K <= S; equivalently the internal state identity carries at most log2(S) bits of distinction.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: K=3 delayed labels with S=2 states.
ceilings.historical_quantity: K pairwise obligation-distinguishable history classes versus S available internal states.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Three pairwise-separated history classes and two states.
ceilings.reproof: If two obligation-distinguishable classes share one complete registered persistent response state, their common continuation yields the same response and one obligation fails. Therefore the class-to-state map is injective.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Myhill-Nerode theorem and distinguishing-set/state lower bounds.

ceilings.falsifier: A policy using only the registered observation achieves zero error while assigning different required actions inside one observation fiber.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For arbitrary sets X,Z,A and maps O:X->Z and g:X->A, a zero-error decoder exists exactly when g factors through O, equivalently when g is constant on every O-fiber.
historical_assumptions: finite deterministic observation map
complete pre-decision information channel is registered
no post-observation probe, intervention, memory, or side information refines the fiber
zero-error required action
ceilings.historical_bound: The required-action partition may not split an observation fiber; independently conditionable latent distinctions are bounded by the observation quotient.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: Two latent states share one observation but require different actions.
ceilings.historical_quantity: Observation equivalence classes induced by the complete registered pre-decision observation map.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Two latent points share an observation but require different actions.
ceilings.reproof: Any decoder pi gives g=pi∘O and therefore equality on fibers. Conversely, fiber constancy defines pi on im(O); extending outside im(O) is irrelevant (or uses a default only when A is nonempty).
ceilings.strongest_parent: Blackwell comparison/sufficiency; deterministic specialization of information garbling and data processing.

ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope B-bit deterministic protocol coordinates K>2^B distinct required receiver actions with zero error.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For arbitrary sender-class set K and registered message carrier M, distinct required receiver actions with no correlated side information require an injection K->M, so |K|<=|M|. The B-bit law is the finite specialization |M|=2^B.
historical_assumptions: finite sender coordination classes
noiseless deterministic fixed-length one-way communication
receiver has no correlated side information about sender class
distinct classes require distinct receiver actions
zero-error coordination
ceilings.historical_bound: B >= ceil(log2 K), or equivalently K <= 2^B distinct zero-error coordination classes.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: K=5 coordination classes over B=2 bits.
ceilings.historical_quantity: K sender classes requiring distinct receiver actions versus a B-bit fixed-length one-way transcript.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Five coordination classes and four messages.
ceilings.reproof: Classes mapped to the same receiver-visible message induce the same receiver action, contradicting distinct requirements. An injective code is sufficient when available.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Deterministic communication complexity; transcript/protocol-tree counting lower bound.

ceilings.falsifier: A fixed in-scope B-bit threshold decoder realizes more than 2^B distinct boundary placements, or covers all N+1 placements when 2^B<N+1.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For arbitrary code carrier C, response-profile set Y, and frozen decoder d:C->Y, the representable profiles are im(d). Covering T requires T subset im(d), equivalently a code preimage for every target; under ordinary choice-based cardinal comparison this gives |T|<=|C|. The old one-threshold/N-point/2^B statement is one finite corollary, not a universal precision ceiling.
historical_assumptions: one-dimensional one-threshold classifier family on a fixed finite ordered probe set
architecture and threshold decoder/codebook are frozen across the target family
all boundary-selecting precision-bearing parameters are included in the B-bit code
no architecture growth, additional high-precision parameter, or task-specific decoder rewrite
zero-error representation of the registered threshold labeling
ceilings.historical_bound: Representable boundary placements <= min(2^B,N+1); complete threshold-family coverage requires B >= ceil(log2(N+1)).
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: N=4 probe points expose five threshold placements but B=2 supplies at most four decoded placements.
ceilings.historical_quantity: N ordered probe points, hence N+1 distinct one-threshold labelings, versus a frozen B-bit threshold code with at most 2^B decoded boundary placements.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Five required profiles, four codes, fixed decoder.
ceilings.reproof: The decoder is a surjection C->im(d). Covering target family T requires selecting at least one preimage code for every target; this yields an injection T->C when finite or when the stated choice principle is available.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Finite hypothesis-class/cardinality counting under parameter quantization; bounded specialization of quantized-network expressivity.

ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic A-symbol, T-event update channel selects K>A^T pairwise target-distinct persistent successor states from the same initial state.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For finite event horizon T and arbitrary registered update alphabets U_t, target-dependent successors selected from one initial state form an image of the transcript product. Under ordinary choice-based cardinal comparison their cardinal is bounded by Π_t |U_t|. Constant finite alphabet A gives A^T.
historical_assumptions: fixed initial persistent state
finite deterministic update alphabet of size A
at most T update events
all target-dependent persistent information enters only through the registered update symbols
no unmetered direct write, external memory mutation, target-correlated side channel, or architecture growth
zero-error target reachability
ceilings.historical_bound: K <= A^T; equivalently T >= ceil(log_A K) when A>1.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: A=2 update symbols for T=2 events expose four transcripts but K=5 distinct successor targets.
ceilings.historical_quantity: K pairwise target-distinct successor states versus an A-symbol persistent update alphabet used for T update events.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Five target-distinct successors through two binary updates.
ceilings.reproof: Target-independent dynamics map each update transcript to at most one successor. Thus successor selection factors through the transcript product; finite cardinality is bounded directly, while the arbitrary-set cardinal comparison uses the stated choice convention.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Finite-alphabet reachability/counting in quantized control and finite-rate information-constrained optimization.

ceilings.falsifier: An exact in-scope protected map of rank R admits more than D-R linearly independent zero-forgetting update directions.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For any finite-dimensional vector space V over any field and linear protected-response map L:V->W, exact protected directions are ker(L), with dim ker(L)=dim V-rank(L). Nonlinear claims are only local when L is an explicit derivative.
historical_assumptions: fixed D-dimensional mutable vector space
protected old behavior is represented by an exact linear map P
retention requires P*Delta=0 exactly
plasticity is counted as the dimension of linearly independent admissible update directions
no architecture growth or auxiliary mutable state outside the registered D coordinates
ceilings.historical_bound: plastic update dimension <= D-R, equivalently protected rank + independent plastic rank <= D.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: D=3 with rank(P)=2 leaves one protected null direction, so a two-dimensional independent plastic update family is impossible without changing protected outputs.
ceilings.historical_quantity: A D-dimensional mutable parameter vector and an exact linear protected-output map P of rank R.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: A rank-two protected map on dimension three cannot contain two independent protected update directions.
ceilings.reproof: Exact first-order retention is L(delta)=0, hence delta lies in ker(L); rank-nullity gives the dimension and a kernel basis attains it.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Rank-nullity theorem; output-preserving/null-space projection methods in continual learning.

ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope planner guarantees complete depth h after inspecting fewer than N(b,h) nodes.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For any registered rooted tree and finite depth h, if every node through h can independently contain the sole decisive event and no pruning certificate, oracle, or merging exists, complete coverage has inspection-cardinality lower bound equal to the entire through-depth-h node set, even when levels are nonuniform or infinite. Sufficiency is set-theoretic; an operational exhaustive procedure additionally needs an enumeration/well-order and completion semantics.
historical_assumptions: finite full b-ary tree and integer horizon h>=0
node inspection is the metered planning resource
any node through depth h may be adversarially decisive
no heuristic oracle, pruning certificate, state merging/transposition, or structural dominance rule
guarantee is complete worst-case coverage, not success on one lucky path
ceilings.historical_bound: N(b,h) <= R. For b>1, h <= floor(log_b(R(b-1)+1))-1; for b=1, h <= R-1.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: A binary tree with R=14 cannot guarantee complete depth 3 because depth 3 contains 15 nodes including the root; R=15 is tight.
ceilings.historical_quantity: Full b-ary planning tree, exhaustive node-inspection budget R, and guaranteed complete horizon h.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Binary depth-two tree, six inspections for seven possible decisive nodes.
ceilings.reproof: Leaving node u unseen makes the no-event world indistinguishable from a world whose sole event is u. Hence every node must be included in the inspected set. The b-ary geometric sum and breadth-first sufficiency are regular finite corollaries.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Uninformed tree-search branching-factor complexity / exhaustive search.

ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic search guarantees the unique valid candidate for all placements with Q<N queries.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For any candidate set C and queried subset Q with |Q|<|C|, if success requires receiving a positive certificate from the unique valid candidate, no strategy restricted to Q guarantees success. Querying all candidates is sufficient only with a traversal/enumeration and completion semantics. If success is mere identification under an exactly-one promise, the finite bound is N-1, so that interpretation of the historical N-query wording is explicitly retracted.
historical_assumptions: finite candidate set with exactly one potentially valid location
validity membership oracle is exact
candidate identities are unstructured and checking one candidate gives no information about another
no generative shortcut, ordering promise, heuristic oracle, side information, or parallel unmetered verification
worst-case zero-error guarantee
ceilings.historical_bound: Worst-case guaranteed verified-solution class size <= Q; complete guarantee over N candidates requires Q>=N.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: N=5 candidates with Q=4 queries; whichever four indices are checked, the fifth can be the unique valid candidate.
ceilings.historical_quantity: N unstructured candidates, one hidden valid candidate, and Q deterministic membership-verifier queries.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Five candidates and four queries: direct verification can fail at the fifth, while identification succeeds under an exactly-one promise.
ceilings.reproof: A strict-subcardinality queried subset omits some c; placing the valid target at c yields only negative answers and no positive certificate. Under the finite exactly-one promise, N-1 negatives identify the sole unqueried point without directly verifying it.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Deterministic decision-tree/query complexity for unstructured search.

ceilings.falsifier: Under the registered exchangeable perfect-check model, measured exact enumeration disagrees with C(M-q,r)/C(M,r), or a q<M deterministic verifier guarantees zero false adoption against an adversarial single defect.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For arbitrary coordinate set I, inspected set S, and probability law mu over defect subsets D, false-adoption probability is mu({D:D∩S=∅}). Distribution-free zero false adoption against singleton defects requires S=I. The hypergeometric ratio is the finite uniform-r-subset specialization.
historical_assumptions: finite M obligation coordinates and 1<=r<=M defects
the r-defect set is uniformly distributed over all r-subsets for the probabilistic bound
q distinct checks are chosen without defect-location side information
each checked defect is detected perfectly
candidate is adopted iff no checked coordinate fails
ceilings.historical_bound: P_FA(q;M,r)=C(M-q,r)/C(M,r). For r=1, P_FA=(M-q)/M. Worst-case adversarial zero-FA requires q=M.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: M=10, r=1, q=8 has exact false-adoption probability 2/10; full q=10 verification has probability 0.
ceilings.historical_quantity: M obligation coordinates, exactly r defective coordinates chosen uniformly among all r-subsets, and q distinct perfect checks without replacement.
ceilings.nearest_hostile: One unchecked coordinate hosts the sole adversarial defect.
ceilings.reproof: Adoption after perfect checks occurs exactly when the defect set avoids S, giving the measure identity. If i is unchecked, the singleton {i} defeats zero-FA; full coverage excludes every nonempty defect set.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Acceptance sampling / hypergeometric sampling without replacement.

ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic q-query protocol identifies K>A^q hypotheses with zero error, or a B-budget protocol with uniform cost c identifies more than A^floor(B/c) hypotheses without another information channel.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For any finite-depth adaptive decision tree with outcome carrier A_v at node v, zero-error hypotheses inject into leaves. Thus distinguishability is bounded by the leaf-set cardinal; a uniform A-ary depth-q tree gives |H|<=|A|^q, for finite or infinite A.
historical_assumptions: finite K latent hypotheses
deterministic noiseless active queries with at most A outcomes each
at most q acquired answers, or uniform positive query cost c under total budget B
no free side information, passive observation or intervention outcome carrying additional target information
zero-error identification; tightness only when the query family can implement a separating code
ceilings.historical_bound: K <= A^q; equivalently q >= ceil(log_A K) for A>1. With uniform cost: K <= A^floor(B/c).
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: Five hypotheses with two binary queries expose at most four transcripts, so exact identification is impossible; three binary queries are sufficient in a rich separating-query family.
ceilings.historical_quantity: K latent hypotheses, at most A outcomes per active query, at most q queries (or total budget B with uniform per-query cost c).
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Five hypotheses but only four transcript leaves.
ceilings.reproof: Two hypotheses ending at one transcript leaf are observationally identical and cannot receive distinct exact labels. Tightness requires the registered query family to realize a separating leaf code.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Decision-tree leaf counting / twenty questions / finite source coding.

ceilings.falsifier: A transcript-only decoder gives different correct responses to two models in the same transcript fiber, or fully identifies two hidden models with identical complete registered transcripts.
ceilings.generalization_beyond_toy_finite_space: For arbitrary hidden-model set Theta, transcript map tau, and required-response map g, exact task response is possible iff g factors through tau. Full model identification is possible iff tau is injective.
historical_assumptions: finite registered hidden agent-model set
complete deterministic social transcript available before the held-out response is frozen
no direct hidden-state label, private-state access or unregistered diagnostic interaction

ceilings.historical_bound: The held-out response partition cannot refine the transcript partition; full identifiable model classes <= number of distinct registered transcripts.
ceilings.historical_negative_twin: Two hidden models produce the same observed action in the base context but require different held-out predictions; no transcript-only decoder can answer both. A registered diagnostic probe that makes their transcripts differ restores identifiability.
ceilings.historical_quantity: Finite hidden agent-model set Theta, registered social observation transcript tau(theta), and held-out required social response g(theta).
ceilings.nearest_hostile: Two hidden models share a complete transcript but require different held-out responses.
ceilings.reproof: This is the arbitrary-set observation-factorization theorem applied to social transcripts; no named agent architecture is used.
ceilings.strongest_parent: The F2 deterministic observation-quotient theorem (direct social-domain corollary), statistical identifiability, and inverse-planning/Bayesian theory-of-mind models that infer hidden goals/beliefs from observed actions.
